description: Real producer exports, and what was measured from them. Separate from the generated manifest one directory up because it is a separate kind of claim: a generated fixture pins a shape of the format and its counts are a property of what was written here, where a recorded file pins what one producer actually exports and its counts are a measurement of someone else's software that nobody here may adjust. Measured fields come from libs/motionBvh/tools/check_corpus.py --recorded, whose scanner is an independent reading of the format rather than a call into the C++ parser. Prose and observations are hand-written. `hierarchy` is measured, not written: it is a reading of the file and not an inference about it, and it is what a row whose bytes this repository does not carry is checked by -- scripts/check_motion_profiles.py holds a producer profile against it when the file itself is absent.
limitations: Every `observations` entry is read OUT of a file that declares none of it. BVH states no unit, no up axis, no handedness, no rotation order and no humanoid bone, so these are evidence for a producer profile to settle -- not facts this layer knows, and not something the parser may act on (docs/roadmap/recorded-motion-sources.md §2).

Nothing measured in one row generalises to another. Each is one session from one application, and the two producers here already disagree about what a root joint is, what an End Site holds, and whether a rig's offsets compose into a pose -- which is exactly why a profile is named `<producer>-<format>-<preset>-v<N>` and why the release condition is two producers rather than one (§3, §8). A third would be evidence about the format; two are evidence that the first one's answers were not it.

A row with `storage: "fetch"` has no bytes here, and its measured fields were taken once, elsewhere, from the file its `sha256` pins. The split is on redistribution and never on worth: this repository is Apache-2.0 and cannot carry data under a licence that restricts what its users may do (§8). `scripts/fetch_corpus.py` puts such a file in `fetched/`, after which every check in the tree treats it exactly like a committed one -- so what is lost while it is absent is one link, that the row is a faithful reading of those bytes, and nothing that depends on the row downstream.

This file is not a shape of the format and does not belong in `generated/`. The two halves are never mixed: a producer's export sitting among the format shapes is the first place one application's answers quietly become the format's definition.

fixtures.pins: The second producer, and the first file here that disagrees with the first one about what a root is. `joint_Root` carries the locomotion -- 157.634 units of Z across 31 frames -- and never rotates; `Hips`, its only child, carries the body's orientation and a translation of its own. So 'where the body is and which way it faces' is split across two joints, where the profile contract has one `root.joint` and the converter reads joint 0 (roadmap §10). It also pins a 30 fps export with position channels on all 22 joints, and a rig with no `upperChest`.
fixtures.redistribution: NOT carried here. CC BY-NC 4.0 permits redistribution with attribution, but only non-commercially, and this repository is Apache-2.0 -- so the bytes stay upstream and this row carries what was measured from them. `scripts/fetch_corpus.py --corpus motion --accept-license bandai-namco-motiondataset` puts the file in recorded/fetched/, where the same scanner re-derives every measured field below and says so if it disagrees.

observations.note: Observed, never declared. Each entry below is what the bytes imply, and every one of them is a producer profile's decision to make rather than this layer's.
observations.channelDeclaration: All 22 joints declare the same six channels in the same order: Xposition Yposition Zposition Zrotation Xrotation Yrotation. The Euler order is therefore ZXY throughout -- the one convention this export shares with the first producer's.
observations.rootMotion: Split across two joints, which is what this file is here for. `joint_Root` translates and never rotates: all three of its rotation columns read 0.000000 in all 31 frames, and its Z sweeps 157.634 units, which is the walk. `Hips`, its only child, carries the body's orientation and a translation of its own spanning about 4 units. Neither joint alone is the root, and taking either one for it loses the other's half.
observations.positionChannels: The 20 joints below `Hips` carry exactly their own OFFSET in all 31 frames -- rest geometry restated every frame, as the first producer's export also does. `Hips` does not: its samples are a position in `joint_Root`'s frame and stand in no relation to its OFFSET.
observations.restOffsets: Bone-local, not world. Every offset runs along +X down its own bone -- Spine (15.7357, 0, 0), Neck (16.3773, 0, 0), LowerLeg_L (39.0811, 0, 0) -- so composing them at identity rotation sends the spine and both legs the same way and produces no figure at all. The joint orientations that reconcile them are inside the rotation channels. Whatever this file's rest pose is, it is not its offsets.
observations.hipsOffset: Per file, not per rig. This file states (0.0408292, 93.9915, 0.0639531) and dataset-2's states (4.5925, 91.4895, -427.239); every other offset in the two agrees to the digit except `LowerLeg_R`. The Hips OFFSET is where the capture volume put the performer, not a property of the skeleton -- so a converter that measured root displacement from it would read 427 cm of Z out of the other file.
observations.upAxis: +Y, from the `Hips` position samples: the column that stays near 92 while the other two wander is the height.
observations.unit: Centimetres, implied: a hip height of 92.1273 in the first frame over an 80.07-unit leg chain (39.0811 thigh + 40.9854 shank).
observations.endSites: Five, and they disagree with dataset-2's five. Here they are 10 or +/-5 along X -- head, hands, toes -- and in dataset-2 every one of them is (0, 0, 0). One producer's own dataset states two different things, so an End Site's contents carry nothing a converter may read, in this export or in general.
observations.humanoidGaps: 22 joints and no fourth torso segment: `Hips`, `Spine`, `Chest`, `Neck`, `Head`, with both shoulders on `Chest`. The canonical humanoid's `upperChest` has nothing to bind to, which is the first rig here that needs a mapping to be optional rather than required.

fixtures.pins: The same rig from the other half of the same dataset, standing still. `joint_Root` holds at 0.000000 in all six channels for all 19 frames, so the split root beside it is a property of the export rather than of one recording -- read alone, this file would say `joint_Root` is a dead node. It also pins the Hips OFFSET as per-file bookkeeping: 427 cm of Z that no sample in the file goes anywhere near.
fixtures.redistribution: NOT carried here, on the terms and by the route the dataset-1 row states.

observations.note: Observed, never declared. Stated here only where this file differs from the dataset-1 row's observations, which otherwise hold for it word for word.
observations.rootMotion: `joint_Root` is motionless: all six of its channels read 0.000000 in all 19 frames. `Hips` still carries the orientation and a translation of its own, beginning at (-0.388099, 82.266300, -0.245212).
observations.hipsOffset: (4.5925, 91.4895, -427.239). The Z is 427 units from every sample in the file, and the same rig in dataset-1 states (0.0408292, 93.9915, 0.0639531) -- the two together are what make this an artefact of the capture rather than a rest translation.
observations.endSites: Five, every one of them (0, 0, 0), where dataset-1's are 10 or +/-5 along X. Same producer, same rig, same field, two answers.

fixtures.pins: The first real producer export this pipeline has read. It pins that the parser handles a full-size export -- 27 joints, 162 columns, 853 rows, scientific-notation values down to 1e-17, a trailing space on every row -- and it is the file the first producer profile was written from (2026-08-05). The session is a standing capture: both arms raised and bent to roughly 90 degrees at the elbow, the head nodding, the body turning about +/-59 degrees around the vertical, and the feet staying put.
fixtures.redistribution: cleared by the capture's owner for publication in this repository (2026-08-04)

observations.note: Observed, never declared. Each entry below is what the bytes imply, and every one of them is a producer profile's decision to make rather than this layer's.
observations.channelDeclaration: All 27 joints declare the same six channels in the same order: Xposition Yposition Zposition Zrotation Xrotation Yrotation. The Euler order is therefore ZXY throughout, and it is stated once per joint rather than assumed anywhere.
observations.positionChannels: The 78 non-root position columns carry exactly their joint's own OFFSET in all 853 frames. They are rest geometry restated every frame, not translation animation; only the root's three columns move.
observations.rootTranslation: Absolute position in the file's own frame, beginning at the root OFFSET (0, 95.9893, 0) in frame 0 -- not a delta, and not zero-based. Over the session it stays within about 7 units laterally.
observations.upAxis: +Y. The root sits at Y 95.9893, the torso chain climbs in +Y and the legs descend in -Y.
observations.forwardAxis: +Z, from the toe End Sites at (0, 0, 0.1).
observations.lateralAxis: +X is the character's left: every l_* joint sits at +X of its parent and every r_* at -X.
observations.handedness: Right-handed, implied by the three axes above rather than declared.
observations.unit: Centimetres, implied: a hip height of 95.9893 over an 81.46-long leg chain (39.89 thigh + 41.57 shank) is a human in centimetres and nothing else.
observations.endSites: Five, each 0.1 along a single axis -- head +Y, hands +/-X, toes +Z. They are direction markers of a fixed length rather than bone extents; a converter that read them as extents would give this skeleton 1 mm hands.
observations.rootJointName: `root`, and there is no joint named `hips` at all. The seven `torso_*` segments are one spine chain, so the mapping onto a VRM humanoid's hips / spine / chest / upperChest is a profile's decision and cannot be recovered from the names. The root is also this rig's hips, which the second producer's export shows to be a coincidence rather than a shape of the format.
